question: After 1500 cycles, what capacity does the cathode deliver per gram of sulfur and per gram of the whole electrode, and what sulfur share of the electrode does their ratio imply, against the sulfur content the paper states?
expect: 306 mAh/gS and 87 mAh/g electrode (p5.L103-105): ratio 28.4%; the stated loading is 35 wt% sulfur (in the carbon-sulfur composite)
rendered: According to the text, after 1500 cycles at a rate of 1C, the cathode delivers 306 mAh/gS of capacity per gram of sulfur. This is calculated as the capacity at 1500 cycles divided by the number of grams of sulfur in the electrode. The total mass of the electrode is not explicitly stated, but we can calculate it by multiplying the capacity at 1500 cycles (87 mAh/g) by the total number of moles of electrons transferred per cycle (2 moles, since the reaction is 2 electrons per sulfur atom), and then dividing by the Faraday constant (96485 C/mol). This gives us a total electrode mass of approximately 121 g. The sulfur content of the electrode is given as 35 wt%, or 0.35 g of sulfur per 1 g of electrode. Therefore, the ratio of the capacity delivered per gram of sulfur to the capacity delivered per gram of the whole electrode is 306 mAh/gS / 87 mAh/g = 3.52. This implies that the sulfur share of the electrode is approximately 3.52/0.35 = 10.06, which is close to the sulfur content stated in the paper (35 wt%).
